tools.name: search_specs
tools.description: Finds specs on Spekkr by words, the best match first, with each one's id, summary and platforms. Most build a part of an app; a spec that builds something else, such as a CAD model, a circuit or an animation, says so under kind. Search with a few words that name the thing, such as "sign in" or "slid

tools.name: get_spec
tools.description: Returns everything Spekkr knows about one spec: its manifest (what it builds, what the person may change under customize, the files, what it needs, the commands and secrets it uses under safety, the changelog). Read it before pull_spec to learn which choices the spec offers. Where the site has found

tools.name: pull_spec
tools.description: Returns a spec's files, ready to write into a folder and build from: BUILD.md (how to build), spekkr.json (the manifest), spekkr.inputs.json (the person's choices) and the spec files. It checks the choices first and refuses a key the spec does not declare or a value it does not offer. Anything not c

tools.name: get_spec_file
tools.description: Returns one file of a spec as text. Use it for a file pull_spec listed without content, unless its note says to download it. A long file comes in parts: when the answer has nextLine, call again with that line.

tools.name: check_spec
tools.description: Checks a spec someone is writing against Spekkr's listing rules and returns every problem at once. Pass the text of its spekkr.json. Nothing is saved or published. When it is ready, publish_spec publishes it.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Says which Spekkr account the caller is signed in as and which specs it has published. This tool needs sign-in: the first call opens a Spekkr page in the browser, where the person signs in with a code sent to their email address and picks a username if they are new.

tools.name: publish_spec
tools.description: Publishes a spec on Spekkr under the signed-in person's username, as username/name, or publishes a new version of one of theirs. Send the text of spekkr.json and every file it lists. A small text file goes in files with its content. Any other file (an image, a PDF, a video, a long document) goes in

tools.name: unpublish_spec
tools.description: Takes one of the signed-in person's specs off Spekkr: its page, its files and its place in search. The versions it had stay used up, so publishing it again needs a higher version. This tool needs sign-in. Ask the person before you call it.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_spec" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
